newsitem.title: USA: May 19-23 NYSE program trading averages 15.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: May 19-23 NYSE program trading averages 15.4 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that program trading by member firms during the week of May 19 through May 23 averaged 15.4 percent of average NYSE daily trading volume of 438.3 million shares, or 67.5 million shares per day.
Program trading accounted for an average of 17.9 percent, or 86 million shares, of the average daily volume of 480.4 million shares during the the week of May 12 through May 16.
In all markets program trading averaged 92.8 million share a day during the week of May 19 through May 23.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program acitivity on the NYSE, the exchange said that BNP Securities, Natwest, Morgan Stanley, Salomon Brothers and Interactive Brokers each executed all or most of its program activity for customers.

Program trading executed by firms as agent,for nonmember customers, totaled 73.1 percent, May 19 through May 23, while volume executed for as principal, for their own accounts amounted to 25.1 percent of program volume.
In the same week, 26.6 percent of program volume related to index arbitrage, while another 1.2 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more, said the exchange.
